title: Consecutive Numbers
statement_md:
Find all numbers that appear at least three times consecutively in the `Logs` table.

Return the result table with column name `ConsecutiveNums` in any order.

Table: `Logs` (`id INT PRIMARY KEY, num INT`)
constraints: id is an autoincrement column starting from 1.

input.schema: CREATE TABLE Logs (id INT PRIMARY KEY, num INT); INSERT INTO Logs VALUES (1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 1), (4, 2), (5, 1), (6, 2), (7, 2);
input.query: SELECT DISTINCT l1.num as ConsecutiveNums FROM Logs l1 JOIN Logs l2 ON l1.id = l2.id - 1 JOIN Logs l3 ON l1.id = l3.id - 2 WHERE l1.num = l2.num AND l2.num = l3.num;

starter_code.sql:
-- Write your PostgreSQL/SQLite query here
SELECT DISTINCT l1.num as ConsecutiveNums
FROM Logs l1
JOIN Logs l2 ON l1.id = l2.id - 1
JOIN Logs l3 ON l1.id = l3.id - 2
WHERE l1.num = l2.num AND l2.num = l3.num;

reference_solution.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT l1.num as ConsecutiveNums
FROM Logs l1
JOIN Logs l2 ON l1.id = l2.id - 1
JOIN Logs l3 ON l1.id = l3.id - 2
WHERE l1.num = l2.num AND l2.num = l3.num;
